notes: Every entry cites where it was confirmed. Add an entry only from PIB Fact Check, a government department or police statement, or reputable reporting of one; never from a social media repost alone.

official_services lists well-known government portals by name so answers can point people to them. The checker's official-domain rule itself is structural (.gov.in and .nic.in, both registrable only by government through NIC), so this list is guidance, not an allow-list.

Debunk kinds: false_claim (the claim itself is false, so a matching message is a warning sign on its own) and channel_warning (a warning about fake links or apps; it counts as a risk only when the message uses an unofficial link, an APK or asks for an OTP, and is otherwise shown as related context).

debunks.summary: Scammers send SMS and WhatsApp messages about pending traffic challans with fake payment links, APK files and PDFs. Check challans only on the official e-Challan portal. Report fraud on 1930.

debunks.topic: Fake e-challan SMS that installs an app
debunks.summary: Kerala Police warned about fake e-challan SMS messages that lead to a malicious APK and give fraudsters control of the phone. Do not install apps from messages.
